Investor-facing; property names such as Santana Row have some local consumer recognition.

First Capital REIT is a Toronto-based real estate investment trust that owns and develops grocery-anchored neighbourhood shopping centers and mixed-use properties in Canada's largest urban centers, such as Toronto, Montreal, Calgary and Vancouver. Tenants include grocers, pharmacies and service retailers. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (FCR.UN). Investor-facing landlord with limited national consumer brand awareness.

Janus Living is a Denver, Colorado senior housing real estate investment company; the Crunchbase description presents it as a REIT-style owner of senior housing communities and Crunchbase shows about $2.9 billion in total funding. Newmark Group is a New York commercial real estate advisory firm offering leasing, capital markets, property and facilities management, valuation and consulting to institutional owners and corporate tenants worldwide. NNN REIT, formerly National Retail Properties, is an Orlando, Florida real estate investment trust that owns more than 3,500 single-tenant net-leased retail properties across the US, tenanted by convenience stores, restaurants, auto service and other chains. RioCan Real Estate Investment Trust is a Toronto-based Canadian REIT owning shopping centers and mixed-use properties in major urban markets, anchored by tenants such as Loblaw, Walmart, Canadian Tire and Cineplex, plus residential developments such as the Well. One of the country's largest REITs, listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (REI.UN). Revenue is rent. Investor-facing with local consumer recognition of its centers.

Safehold is a New York REIT that owns ground leases, long-term leases on the land underneath commercial and multifamily buildings, giving property owners a way to unlock value from land. Managed under the iStar and Safehold heritage and now an independent listed company on the NYSE (SAFE), with a ground lease portfolio valued at around $7 billion. Investor-facing, no consumer brand.

Saudi Real Estate Refinance Company (SRC) is a Riyadh-based government-backed mortgage refinancing company, owned by the Public Investment Fund, that provides long-term financing to banks and finance companies to support home ownership in Saudi Arabia under the Vision 2030 housing program. about: Simon Property Group is an Indianapolis-based REIT and the largest US mall operator, owning premium malls and outlets such as Roosevelt Field, King of Prussia and Premium Outlets, with international interests in Asia and Europe. Tenants are major retailers; revenue is above $6 billion in rent. Listed on the NYSE (SPG). Its malls are visited by tens of millions of shoppers, giving real consumer reach.

Vanke (China Vanke) is a Shenzhen-based property developer, one of China's largest, building residential communities and commercial, logistics and rental housing across Chinese cities, and a service business (Wanwu). Listed in Shenzhen (000002) and Hong Kong (2202); Shenzhen Metro became its largest shareholder, and it has faced debt stress since 2021 along with the property downturn. Revenue was tens of billions of dollars. Known consumer brand in China's housing market.

Vonovia is Germany's largest residential landlord, based in Bochum, owning and managing over 500,000 apartments in Germany, Sweden and Austria, and offering related services such as energy supply and maintenance. Tenants are private households; revenue is rent. Formed through the 2015 merger with Deutsche Annington and Gagfah. Listed in Frankfurt (VNA) and a DAX member. A large and well-known name in German housing, but not a consumer product brand.

W. P. Carey is a New York net-lease REIT, founded in 1973, that owns a diversified portfolio of industrial, warehouse, retail and office properties leased to corporate tenants in North America and Europe under long-term leases, plus an investment management business. Carmila is a Paris-based French owner and manager of shopping centres adjacent to Carrefour hypermarkets in France, Spain and Italy, formed in 2014 by Carrefour and institutional investors. It earns rent from retailers in about 200 centres. Listed on Euronext Paris (CARM). Investor-facing landlord, though its malls are widely visited by shoppers.

Five Holdings is a Dubai-based real estate and hospitality investment firm, owner of FIVE Hotels and Resorts brands including FIVE Palm Jumeirah, FIVE Jumeirah Village and Zurich properties, with a boutique lifestyle focus. Crunchbase shows about $1 billion in funding. Consumer-facing hospitality brand with a strong nightlife and event profile in Dubai.

New World Development is a Hong Kong property developer and investor with residential, commercial and retail properties in Hong Kong and mainland China, including K11 shopping and art malls, Victoria Dockside and the Grand Hyatt Hong Kong. It is part of the Cheng family's empire, led by Adrian Cheng and chairman Henry Cheng, and is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (0017). It has faced heavy debt pressure and refinancing in recent years. It is a major Hong Kong consumer real estate and retail brand.

American Homes 4 Rent is a US real estate investment trust that owns and operates single-family homes for rent, with about 60,000 homes across 20-plus states, concentrated in the Southeast, Midwest and Texas. It earns rental income from residents and has a development programme building homes to rent. It is based in Agoura Hills, California, listed on the NYSE (AMH), and founded by B. Wayne Hughes. It is a consumer housing brand with moderate awareness among renters.

Country Garden is a Chinese property developer, headquartered in Foshan, Guangdong with a Hong Kong listing (2007), which was once China's biggest by sales, building residential communities in hundreds of cities. Since 2023 it has been in a debt crisis, defaulted on offshore bonds and has been restructuring its liabilities. It also has a property management arm, Country Garden Services. It is a household name among Chinese homebuyers, and a distressed company with significant reputational and financial risk.

Global Net Lease is a New York based real estate investment trust that owns a portfolio of net leased commercial properties, such as office, industrial and retail buildings, leased to corporate tenants in the US, the UK and Western Europe on long-term triple-net leases. It is externally managed by AR Global and listed on the NYSE (GNL). In 2024-2025 it sold its multi-tenant retail portfolio to refocus on core properties. It is a B2B property investor with limited consumer awareness.

Healthpeak Properties is a Denver, Colorado real estate investment trust that owns life science laboratory, outpatient medical and senior housing (CCRC) real estate, leased to biotech companies, health systems and operators in the US. It was previously HCP, founded in 1985, and is listed on the NYSE (DOC). Its market value is in the range of 12 to 15 billion dollars. It is a B2B real estate investor with little consumer brand awareness.

ROSHN is a Riyadh based Saudi real estate developer owned by the Public Investment Fund (PIF), building large residential communities such as Sarai in Riyadh, Warefa and the Alarous districts, as part of Saudi Vision 2030 housing goals. It sells homes and community facilities to Saudi families, and is already a sports sponsor: it is title sponsor of the Roshn Saudi League and a global partner of Formula 1. Funding shown is about SAR 11 billion. It is a prominent state-backed consumer property brand.

Sunac China Holdings is a Chinese property developer, listed in Hong Kong (1918), which has residential projects across China and had a big presence in Tianjin. It has been in a major debt crisis since 2021, defaulted on offshore bonds and has been restructuring its debts. It once owned stakes in Leshi (LeEco) and Wanda's tourism assets. It is a household name for Chinese homebuyers, and is a distressed company with significant financial risk.

Tishman Speyer is a New York based real estate developer, owner and operator of offices, residential, retail and mixed-use projects around the world, including Rockefeller Center, which it owns, the Chrysler Building previously and projects across Europe, Asia and Latin America. Founded in 1978 and led by Rob Speyer, it manages tens of billions of dollars of assets and runs investment funds. It is private. It is a prominent B2B real estate brand with a visible presence in global cities.

Aura Holdings is an Australian property developer based in Coorparoo, Brisbane, and is known for Aura City on the Sunshine Coast, a large master-planned community in the Caloundra South area. Regional developer, with brand awareness in Queensland.

B2B landlord with low consumer brand awareness.

Choice Properties REIT is Canada's largest real estate investment trust, owning and managing about 700 retail, industrial, office and residential properties, mostly grocery-anchored retail leased to Loblaw Companies. B2B landlord; the Loblaw and No Frills brands are what consumers know.

Compass is a US residential real estate brokerage and technology platform, founded in 2012, whose agents buy and sell homes using its software for marketing, client management and listings. Headquartered in New York and listed on the NYSE (COMP). Strong B2C brand in affluent US markets.

Diriyah Company is the Saudi giga-project developer behind Diriyah, the historic Najdi heritage site on the edge of Riyadh, which includes At-Turaif (UNESCO World Heritage). It is developing a multibillion-dollar mixed-use destination with hotels, retail, cultural and residential space, owned by the Public Investment Fund. Customers will be visitors, residents, tenants and investors. Based in Riyadh. Hosted the Formula E in Diriyah and is a visible Saudi tourism and sports presence.

First Industrial Realty Trust is a US real estate investment trust that owns, develops and manages industrial and logistics properties, around 400 buildings of roughly 65 million sq ft, in major markets such as Southern California, Dallas, Atlanta and Chicago. Getty Realty is a US real estate investment trust that owns convenience and automotive retail properties, mainly gas stations and car washes leased to operators, with over 1,000 sites across around 40 states. B2B landlord with low consumer brand awareness.
